deck.name: The Human Body
deck.description: Organs, bones, blood, senses and the systems that keep you going.

questions.prompt: What is the largest organ of the human body?
questions.explanation: Skin covers the body and helps protect it, sense the surroundings and regulate temperature.

questions.prompt: Which organ pumps blood through the body?
questions.explanation: The heart's muscular walls contract to move blood through the lungs and the rest of the body.

questions.prompt: Which part of blood carries most of its oxygen?
questions.explanation: Hemoglobin inside red blood cells binds oxygen. A small amount of oxygen also dissolves in plasma.

questions.prompt: Arteries always carry blood away from the heart.
questions.explanation: Direction defines an artery. The pulmonary arteries carry oxygen-poor blood from the heart to the lungs.

questions.prompt: How many chambers does a typical human heart have?
questions.explanation: The heart has two upper chambers called atria and two lower chambers called ventricles.

questions.prompt: Where does most oxygen enter the blood in the lungs?
questions.explanation: Alveoli are tiny air sacs surrounded by capillaries. Oxygen and carbon dioxide cross their thin walls.

questions.prompt: Which muscle below the lungs does most of the work of quiet breathing?
questions.explanation: The diaphragm contracts and moves downward when you breathe in, increasing the space inside the chest.

questions.prompt: The left lung is usually larger than the right lung.
questions.explanation: The heart takes up space on the left side of the chest.

questions.prompt: Where are most nutrients from food absorbed?
questions.explanation: The small intestine's lining has folds and tiny projections that provide a large surface for absorption.

questions.prompt: Which organ makes bile?
questions.explanation: The liver makes bile, which helps the body digest and absorb fats.

questions.prompt: Which organ stores and concentrates bile between meals?
questions.explanation: The gallbladder releases stored bile into the small intestine when it is needed.

questions.prompt: Which organ produces insulin?
questions.explanation: Beta cells in the pancreas make insulin, a hormone that helps regulate blood glucose.

questions.prompt: Which tube carries swallowed food from the throat to the stomach?
questions.explanation: Waves of muscle contraction called peristalsis move food along the esophagus.

questions.prompt: Which organs filter blood to remove wastes and make urine?
questions.explanation: Kidneys also help regulate the body's water, salts and acid balance.

questions.prompt: Where is urine stored before it leaves the body?
questions.explanation: Ureters carry urine to the bladder. The urethra carries it out of the body.

questions.prompt: Which is the longest bone in the human body?
questions.explanation: The femur is the thigh bone. It runs from the hip to the knee.

questions.prompt: What is the anatomical name for the kneecap?
questions.explanation: The patella sits within a tendon at the front of the knee.

questions.prompt: Which is the smallest bone in the human body?
questions.explanation: The stapes is one of three tiny middle-ear bones that pass sound vibrations toward the inner ear.

questions.prompt: What usually connects a skeletal muscle to a bone?
questions.explanation: Tendons transmit the force of a muscle's contraction to bone.

questions.prompt: What usually connects one bone to another at a joint?
questions.explanation: Ligaments help stabilize joints. Tendons usually connect muscles to bones.

questions.prompt: Which part of the brain helps coordinate movement and balance?
questions.explanation: The cerebellum helps fine-tune movements and maintain posture and balance.

questions.prompt: What is the opening in the center of the iris called?
questions.explanation: The iris changes the pupil's size to control how much light enters the eye.

questions.prompt: Which layer at the back of the eye contains light-sensitive cells?
questions.explanation: Retinal photoreceptors convert light into signals that travel toward the brain.

questions.prompt: Which inner-ear structure contains the sensory hair cells used for hearing?
questions.explanation: The cochlea is a fluid-filled spiral. Its hair cells help turn vibrations into signals for the auditory nerve.

questions.prompt: Where are most blood cells made in a healthy adult?
questions.explanation: Red bone marrow contains blood-forming stem cells. Yellow marrow mainly stores fat.

questions.prompt: Which blood components form the initial plug at a damaged blood vessel?
questions.explanation: Platelets stick to the injured area and each other. Clotting proteins then help reinforce the plug with fibrin.

questions.prompt: What covers the visible crown of a healthy tooth?
questions.explanation: Enamel is the hard outer layer of the crown. Dentin lies beneath it, while cementum covers the root.

questions.prompt: Sweat cools the body mainly by evaporating from the skin.
questions.explanation: Evaporation takes heat from the skin. Sweat that drips off without evaporating provides much less cooling.

questions.prompt: What is a neuron?
questions.answer: A nerve cell that receives and sends information using electrical and chemical signals.

questions.prompt: What is homeostasis?
questions.answer: The regulation of internal conditions, such as temperature and blood glucose, within ranges that support normal body function.
